rubbing-alcohol.classifiedAs: Hazards of 2-propanol (isopropyl alcohol) of 40% to 90% in water, from a supplier's safety data sheet

statements: H225: Highly flammable liquid and vapor
H336: May cause drowsiness or dizziness

note.value:
The rubbing alcohol here is about 70% 2-propanol in water, a few millilitres in a tube. The supplier's sheet for that strength keeps it from heat, sparks, flames and hot surfaces, and from strong oxidizers and acids; has it used in a hood or a well-ventilated room; and calls for eye protection, gloves and protective clothing. It says that drinking it can kill. The one acid it meets on this bench is vinegar, in a tube.

Stricter, and what this lab goes by: NOAA's record of the alcohol says that the vapour is heavier than air and can reach a flame some way off and flash back; that splashed skin is flooded with water while the clothing comes off; and, for the eyes, flushing with water for 20 to 30 minutes and a hospital after.

How any of it is disposed of is decided by the laboratory's own rules and by local regulations; ask the laboratory's supervisor.

mineral-oil.classifiedAs: Hazards of mineral oil, from a supplier's safety data sheet

note.value:
The mineral oil is a few millilitres in a tube. The supplier's sheet prints no signal word and no hazard statement, and calls this oil, kept beside chemicals that are not food, not for use on the skin. It keeps the oil from eyes and clothing, with hands washed after. It calls the oil combustible, and a spill slippery.

Stricter, and what this lab goes by: NOAA's record calls the oil mildly irritating to the eyes, says its vapour or droplets breathed in can bring on pneumonia, and that it can cause dermatitis: it is kept off the skin, and washed off with soap and water. If any is swallowed, no one is made to vomit; a poison centre or doctor is called at once if any reached the lungs. Eyes are rinsed with water for several minutes.

How any of it is disposed of is decided by the laboratory's own rules and by local regulations; ask the laboratory's supervisor.
